messages:
anya: Heads up — noticed a ~12% drop in early-context prefix hit-rate after yesterday's kernel-fusion rollout to canaries. Metrics from canary cluster A -> B look divergent.
ryan: ugh. which metric exactly? prefix hits or overall token efficiency? :thinking_face:
anya: prefix_hit_rate (per-route, 95p) and effective tokens-per-request. Here are the canary diffs from last 6h:
```
route: /chat/compose
baseline: prefix_hit_rate=0.78 -> canary: 0.66
avg_tokens/request baseline: 45 -> canary: 53
latency p95 baseline: 120ms -> canary: 135ms
```
ryan: that gap is substantial. did the rollout include the vectorized-attn pack4/pack8 mix + quant profile swap?
anya: yes — rolled fused-kernel v2.3 (fusion + pack4) and applied the new quant profile q8_pack4_v1. We also changed the kernel allocator alignment, per release notes.
infra-bot: deploy: fused-kernel-v2.3 -> canary-A/2026-03-17T23:40Z
sasha: quick thought: cache keying is sensitive to tokenizer normalization and padding order. Any checksum/fingerprint changes in the input->prefix-key pipeline?
anya: ran a quick diff of the key fingerprints for a sample of 10k requests. ~11% of keys changed value after the new kernel (same input). Example:
```
old_fingerprint: ab12c3f9
new_fingerprint: ab12c3f9  <-- same for 89%
new_fingerprint: ab12c3f0  <-- changed for 11%
```
ryan: interesting. that suggests nondeterminism or a different preproc ordering introduced by the fused path. Could be buffer padding or trailing null bytes affecting hash. Where do we compute the fingerprint now? pre-tokenizer layer or after tokenization?
anya: prefix key is built from: (model_version, user_id_hash, tokenizer_norm(text), tokenizer_tokens[:64]) — fingerprint computed in runtime/kv_key.cc using xxhash on the joined byte array.
eve: did anyone check whether tokenization boundaries shifted (subword splits) due to a tokenizer micro-change bundled in the runtime compile?
anya: tokenizer code didn't change. But the runtime now uses a vectorized token packer that pads tokens to 4-wide lanes before hashing to keep alignment for fused kernels. That pad step may be introduced only on the fused path prior to key construction.
chris: if padding is happening before key hash, that would flip keys. We should canonicalize key creation to always strip pad bytes before hashing. Short patch idea: compute key on trimmed tokens buffer (trim trailing PAD_IDs) and keep key derivation identical across kernels.
ryan: agree. short-term mitigation: revert kernel on canary or enable fallback kernel for prefix-key route only. Long-term: make key derivation kernel-agnostic.
anya: repro steps I used:
1) curl -H "x-canary: A" to 10k prompts
2) dump prefix_key from /internal/kv/debug for matching request ids
3) compare hashes
I can push anonymized sample of mismatched keys to S3 if you want.
sasha: please do. also collect the small binary blobs of pre-hash bytes — we need to confirm whether it's padding vs subtle unicode norm differences.
eve: also check if q8_pack4 quant changes introduced any deterministic rounding that affects tokenizer output feed (unlikely but worth checking). A/B the runtime with pack4 disabled.
anya: quick workaround deployed to canary: enabled fallback-to-legacy-hash (flag runtime.prefetch.canonicalize_keys=true) — hit-rate recovered to ~0.77 within ~20m. I left the flag on for canary-A.
infra-bot: flag set: runtime.prefetch.canonicalize_keys=true for canary-A
ryan: good sanity check. action items:
- anya: upload sample mismatched pre-hash blobs + key diffs to s3://redwood-dev/eng-runtime/prefix-drift/1719999999
- chris: prototype trim-pad-before-hash patch and smoke test
- sasha: run tokenizer/token-breakdown on those samples to rule out tokenization drift
- eve: validate quant profile isolation (run pack4-disabled build on canary)

anya: timeline: if patch looks good we can keep v2.3 in canary with canonicalize_keys=false later and schedule a canary re-roll; if not, prepare to roll v2.3 back from prod tomorrow morning.
ryan: add a notice to #eng-releases and alert SRE to watch the affected customer routes. I'll start the rollback runbook draft in case we need it.
anya: thanks — will post S3 link in this thread in ~30m. :thumbsup:
